forecasts.question: Will the June 17 MOU 60-day negotiating window receive a formal announced extension beyond EOD 2026-08-16, confirmed jointly by Iran and at least one named mediator (Oman, Pakistan, or Qatar)?
forecasts.delta_reason: Pakistan Interior Minister Naqvi in Tehran Aug 12 for 'final push' ahead of Aug 16 deadline; Iran held firm on Rezaei six conditions per Al Jazeera. MOU text specifies window 'extendable with mutual consent.' No extension framework announced as of EOD Aug 12. Three days remain. Base rate for last-minute MOU renewals in this conflict: zero (June ceasefire extension required new mediation round).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named Iranian official (FM, SNSC secretary, or president) and a named mediator (Oman, Pakistan, or Qatar FM or equivalent) jointly or simultaneously announce the MOU negotiating window is extended beyond Aug 16, 2026, with a new end date or duration specified.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) plus Iran MFA/IRNA or mediator FM official readout confirming joint extension.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral Iranian announcement without named mediator co-confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. MOU informally treated as 'continuing' without joint public announcement of extension = NO. Mediator alone announces extension without Iran MFA confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Pakistan FM Naqvi issues joint statement with Araghchi announcing MOU window extension with new stated date
indicators.expected_effect: +40pp toward YES — joint mediator + Iran confirmation is the resolution-criteria trigger

indicators.name: Oman FM confirms MOU negotiating window extended beyond Aug 16 with new end date specified
indicators.expected_effect: +35pp toward YES — alternative mediator channel achieving the same joint-confirmation threshold

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran publicly announce a signed interim Hormuz commercial-shipping framework agreement before EOD 2026-08-19?
forecasts.delta_reason: On Aug 11–12, SNSC chief Rezaei issued six non-negotiable conditions for Hormuz reopening (cessation of US military operations, end of naval blockade, US force withdrawal, full war-damage compensation, sanctions lift, release of ~$24bn frozen assets) and explicitly decoupled any Oman-Iran navigation corridor text from the broader commercial reopening — removing the scenario under which F1 could resolve YES without a fundamental reversal of both declaratory positions. Trump on Aug 12 posted 'total control' and 'wall of steel,' with no withdrawal of Aug 10 compensation demand. Pakistan Naqvi visited Tehran Aug 12 for a 'final push'; Iran held firm on all conditions. All three F1 indicators are now CONTRADICTED. Six days remain to the Aug 19 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a publicly confirmed signed interim framework agreement on Hormuz commercial shipping transit is announced by both the US and Iranian governments (or their named principals/representatives) before EOD 2026-08-19. A joint statement or named mediator (Oman FM, Qatar FM) announcement of a signed and mutually acknowledged text qualifies. Unilateral US or Iranian declarations of deal terms without the other side's public confirmation do NOT qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Axios/Al Jazeera) plus either US State Dept or Iranian MFA/IRNA confirming the same instrument.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreed-in-principle or 'framework agreed' announcements without a signed text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iran-Oman bilateral shipping-route coordination agreement without explicit named US co-acknowledgment of the same instrument = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iran parliament passes any rival Hormuz control bill that contradicts or supersedes the Oman-channel corridor text = NO. If one side announces and the other denies within 24h, treat as NO unless clarified by both parties.

indicators.name: Oman FM readout confirming signed Hormuz text with named US and Iranian co-signatures
indicators.expected_effect: +35pp toward YES — Oman FM readout with both-side named co-acknowledgment meets the bilateral confirmation threshold

indicators.name: Trump publicly withdraws or substantially redefines Aug 10 compensation demand
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES — withdrawal of the Aug 10 demand removes a structurally new pre-condition added after prior negotiating frameworks

indicators.name: Iran MFA confirms acceptance of Oman-channel corridor text without additional pre-conditions
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES — Iran MFA acceptance without pre-conditions would be a necessary condition for YES resolution

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed formally convened US-Iran negotiating session (direct or Oman/Qatar/Pakistan-mediated) occur before EOD 2026-08-26?
forecasts.delta_reason: Araghchi stated Aug 9 that Iran and the US conduct only an 'exchange of messages' through intermediaries — explicitly not negotiations, which F2's own ambiguity rule classifies as non-qualifying. On Aug 11–12, Rezaei issued six preconditions constituting structural prerequisites Iran has never previously demanded before a convened session. Pakistan Naqvi visited Tehran Aug 12; Iran held firm, no session announced. The Oman mediation committee has held no sessions since Iranian strikes on Oman in July (~18 Omani nationals killed, 23 injured); operationally inactive. Last formally convened session: Islamabad, April 11–12, 2026 — 124 days ago. Thirteen days remain to the Aug 26 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US principals (Witkoff or equivalent) and named Iranian principals (Araghchi or equivalent), hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Qatar/Pakistan), before EOD 2026-08-26.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/CNN/Al Jazeera plus confirmation from either US State Dept or Iran MFA/IRNA of the same session.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Relay of written messages, draft texts, or corridor coordinates through intermediaries without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Unilateral assertion of 'ongoing talks' without mediator or counterpart confirmation = NO.

indicators.name: Oman FM convenes named session with US and Iranian envoys and issues a readout
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES — Oman FM convening with named principals on both sides is the clearest direct resolution signal

indicators.name: Mohsen Rezaei (SNSC secretary) or designated Iranian negotiating principal publicly endorses resumption of Oman-channel formal session
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES — SNSC endorsement of formal session would signal the six-condition prerequisite was suspended or waived

indicators.name: Trump publicly withdraws the Aug 10 compensation demand
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES — withdrawal of the structurally new US pre-condition would remove one barrier to a convened session

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz commercial transit volume reach >=40 vessels/day (7-day moving average) before EOD 2026-09-30?
forecasts.delta_reason: Lloyd's List Hormuz Brief Aug 12 recorded 78 commercial transits for the week Aug 3–9 — approximately 11 vessels/day on a 7-day moving average — down from 95 the prior week (~13.5/day), moving in the wrong direction. JMIC threat level remained at SUBSTANTIAL as of Advisory Update 082 (Aug 9); no further downgrade since Aug 5. Rezaei on Aug 12 explicitly stated any Oman-Iran corridor text would NOT constitute a strait reopening, removing the primary near-term pathway to commercial volume recovery. At ~11/day the current rate is 28% of the 40/day target; transit declined week-over-week with all leading indicators static or deteriorating.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch or equivalent AIS aggregator (MarineTraffic, Lloyd's List Intelligence, Bloomberg shipping) records >=40 commercial vessel transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-09-30.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Lloyd's List Intelligence Hormuz Brief plus one of: IMF PortWatch, Bloomberg shipping data, or Reuters/AP/AFP shipping report confirming the same 7-day average.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Military or naval vessels do not count toward commercial transit total. Navy-escorted commercial convoys count as commercial transits. If PortWatch is unavailable, use best AIS source and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources diverge by more than 20%. Isolated single-day surges without a qualifying 7-day rolling average = NO.

indicators.name: Lloyd's List records 7-day average of >=25 transits/day (leading indicator toward 40)
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES — reaching 25/day would establish a recoverable trend toward the 40/day threshold

indicators.name: JMIC downgrades Hormuz threat level from SUBSTANTIAL to MODERATE
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES — MODERATE designation is the threshold at which P&I cover reinstatement typically accelerates

indicators.name: Lloyd's P&I war-risk cover reinstated for Hormuz commercial transit
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES — cover reinstatement is the gating commercial condition for bulk operator re-routing from Cape of Good Hope to Hormuz

forecasts.question: Will Iran's parliament (Majlis) pass the Strait of Hormuz governance bill in a full plenary floor vote before EOD 2026-09-30?
forecasts.delta_reason: Parliamentary National Security and Foreign Policy Committee approved bill framework unanimously Aug 9 (zero opposing votes — Iran International described this as unusual even for politically sensitive legislation). Internal Affairs Committee simultaneously approved provision barring US and Israeli vessel transit with fines up to 20% of cargo value. Full plenary floor vote plus Guardian Council review required for enactment. Unanimous committee approval across two parallel tracks, SNSC/IRGC institutional alignment, and 48-day plenary window. Bill could be tactically delayed (Iran may prefer the threat over the law), keeping probability below 0.65.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran's full Majlis plenary session votes to approve the Hormuz governance bill on the floor record, as reported by official Iranian parliamentary speaker or IRNA, before EOD 2026-09-30.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IRNA or official Majlis speaker statement confirming plenary vote result, plus one TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Iran International) confirming the same vote.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Committee approval only (already achieved Aug 9–10) = NO, the question requires plenary passage. Guardian Council rejection after plenary passage does not retroactively reverse YES on this question. Substantial modification removing the US/Israeli vessel-barring provision before plenary vote = AMBIGUOUS.

indicators.name: Majlis speaker schedules full plenary debate on Hormuz governance bill with date in official calendar
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES — official scheduling marks the transition from committee to plenary track and establishes a binding timeline

indicators.name: Iran International or IRNA reports plenary vote tally or outcome on Hormuz governance bill
indicators.expected_effect: +45pp toward YES — direct TIER1 or IRNA confirmation of a plenary vote is the resolution trigger

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran publicly sign a comprehensive peace/nuclear framework agreement covering nuclear enrichment limits, Hormuz freedom of navigation, and a sanctions roadmap before EOD 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: All near-term dependencies deteriorated this cycle: F1 collapsed to 0.08 and F2 to 0.18 as both declaratory positions hardened. Rezaei's six conditions — including full sanctions lift and end of the war as prerequisites — are structurally incompatible with the US 'total control' and compensation-demand positions. Iran's parliamentary committee unanimously approved the Hormuz governance bill framework Aug 9–10; if N2 resolves YES, it creates a domestic legal constraint on any future Iranian executive accepting a narrower deal. MOU 60-day negotiating window expires Aug 16 with no extension announced. IAEA nuclear inspections remain blocked. Iranian strikes on Oman in July damaged the primary mediation channel's operational depth.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a publicly confirmed signed comprehensive agreement is jointly announced by the US and Iranian governments, covering all three domains: (1) Iran nuclear enrichment limits or elimination; (2) Hormuz freedom of navigation guarantee; (3) US sanctions relief roadmap — before EOD 2026-10-27.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept and Iran MFA/IRNA joint or simultaneous announcement plus two TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN) confirming all three domains are covered.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Hormuz-only interim deal without nuclear or sanctions elements = NO. Nuclear-only deal without Hormuz = NO. Agreed-in-principle without a signed text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. MOU extension or renewal without new nuclear commitments = NO.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES — a convened session would reopen the structured negotiating architecture required for a comprehensive deal

indicators.name: F1 (Hormuz interim deal signed) resolves YES and holds for >=2 weeks without new Iranian attacks on commercial shipping
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES — a durable Hormuz interim deal would demonstrate sufficient mutual trust for comprehensive talks

indicators.name: Iran formally accepts zero-enrichment or cap-enrichment as negotiating basis in named-official statement
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES — Iran formally accepting enrichment limits is a necessary condition for the nuclear domain of any comprehensive agreement
